study.brief_markdown:
## Question

What are the solar and efficiency upgrade opportunities for property 23453 [E1]?

## Property

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Name | Halstead [E1] |
| Address | 4620 [E1] N [E1] Braeswood [E1] Blvd [E1], Houston [E1], TX [E1] 77096 [E1] |
| Owner | JRK Property Holdings [E1] |
| Building size | 389004.0 [E1] sq ft |
| Year built | 1965 [E1] |
| Total units | 592 [E1] |
| Surface parking spaces | 350 [E1] |

## Aerial Inspection

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Measured roof area | 40956.0 [E4] sq ft |
| Usable roof area for solar | 18430.0 [E6] sq ft |
| Parking spaces (central property) | 0 [E4] |
| Green cover | 12.0 [E4] % |
| Paved surface | 55.0 [E4] % |
| AC units detected | 16 [E2] |
| Roof vents detected | 43 [E2] |
| Roof condition | Flat membrane [E2] with 10.96 [E2] % water pooling discoloration |
| Confidence | 62 [E4] % |

## Interior

Matterport model available [E5]. Scanned floor area: 672.6 [E5] sq ft (1 [E5] floor, 10 [E5] rooms). Measured ceiling heights: 8.92 [E5] ft (primary rooms), 7.51 [E5] ft (secondary). Kitchen-living area: 302.94 [E5] sq ft. Bedroom: 154.11 [E5] sq ft. Measured rooms available; interior images not assessed [E5].

## Recommended Upgrades

| Upgrade | Status | kW | Annual kWh | Payback Years | Notes |
|---------|--------|-----|------------|---------------|-------|
| Rooftop solar | Estimated [E7] | 221.2 [E6] | 308475.0 [E6] | 15.9 [E6] | Cost: $442,325 [E6]; Annual savings: $27,763 [E6] |
| Solar carport | Not estimated [E7] | — | — | — | No known surface parking space count [E7] |
| LED lighting | Not estimated [E7] | — | — | — | Needs lighting fixture inventory, wattage, operating hours; Matterport records no fixtures [E7] |
| Window film | Not estimated [E7] | — | — | — | Needs glazing area, orientation, cooling load; aerial imagery does not show facades [E7] |
| HVAC upgrade | Not estimated [E7] | — | — | — | Needs equipment type, age, efficiency data; many rooftop obstructions detected [E7] |

## Assumptions

Solar analysis (E6 [E6]):
- Usable roof fraction: 45 [E6] % of measured roof
- Solar density: 12.0 [E6] watts per usable sq ft
- Installed cost: $2.00 [E6] per watt
- Electricity price: $0.09 [E6] per kWh (state average)
- System tilt: 10 [E6] degrees
- System azimuth: 180 [E6] degrees (south-facing)
- System losses: 14 [E6] %
- Energy source: NREL PVWatts v8 [E6]
- No incentives applied [E6]

Upgrade screening assumptions [E7]:
- Simple payback ranking [E7]
- Estimated upgrades ranked by payback; unestimated upgrades listed separately [E7]

## Risks and Limitations

1. **Aerial imagery uncertainty**: Roof area measured from aerial image [E6] may include roof areas that cannot hold panels due to obstructions, penetrations, or structural constraints [E6].

2. **Simple payback methodology**: Payback [E6] is simple payback with no financing, tax incentives, degradation, demand charges [E6], or operating and maintenance costs [E6]. This is a screening estimate, not a complete financial feasibility assessment [E7].

3. **Interior scan limitations**: Matterport model [E5] provides measured floor dimensions and room counts but no interior images [E5], so lighting type, window characteristics, and visible HVAC equipment were not assessed [E5].

4. **Limited upgrade coverage**: Four of five screened upgrades could not be estimated [E7]. Solar carport requires known parking spaces (none found for central property) [E7]. LED lighting and window film need detailed inventory data not available from aerial imagery [E7]. HVAC assessment is only indicative from roof obstruction counts [E7].

5. **Data sources**: Inputs come from aerial imagery and CoStar records [E7]; an on-site assessment and utility bills are needed for validation [E7].

6. **Roof measurements**: Image-measured roof area [E4] is from aerial imagery approximately 100 [E4] m across the property point and may not reflect exact legal parcel boundaries [E4].

## Next Steps

The draft owner email is ready for human review and has not been sent. Please review the email body below before any outreach.

The CityLab team
